report_name: Medusa Ransomware Has Breached Over 500 Critical Infrastructure Orgs

threat_actors.name: Medusa
threat_actors.description: A Ransomware-as-a-Service (RaaS) group that has compromised over 500 organizations since June 2021. The group targets critical infrastructure sectors using a double-extortion model, encrypting data and leaking it on a dark web site if the ransom is not paid. Affiliates gain access via initial access brokers and by exploiting unpatched vulnerabilities.
threat_actors.goals: Financial extortion through ransomware and data exfiltration.

attack_patterns.name: Phishing
attack_patterns.description: Medusa affiliates use phishing to steal credentials for initial access.

attack_patterns.name: Exploit Public-Facing Application
attack_patterns.description: Medusa affiliates compromise vulnerable, internet-facing servers for initial access, sometimes exploiting vulnerabilities like CVE-2026-1731 within 24 hours of disclosure.

attack_patterns.name: Remote Access Software
attack_patterns.description: Medusa actors deploy and use legitimate remote monitoring and management (RMM) software such as AnyDesk, Splashtop, and Atera to maintain persistence and evade detection.

attack_patterns.name: Exfiltration Over C2 Channel
attack_patterns.description: Before encryption, sensitive data is exfiltrated to attacker-controlled storage to enable a double-extortion tactic.

attack_patterns.name: Data Encrypted for Impact
attack_patterns.description: The Medusa ransomware payload is deployed to encrypt files across the victim network, demanding a ransom for decryption.

attack_patterns.name: Inhibit System Recovery
attack_patterns.description: Medusa actors were observed using the command 'vssadmin.exe delete shadows /all /quiet' to delete volume shadow copies, preventing system recovery from backups.

attack_patterns.name: Remote Desktop Protocol
attack_patterns.description: The advisory notes that Medusa actors use RDP for lateral movement.

malware.name: Medusa Ransomware
malware.description: The primary payload used by the Medusa group. It encrypts files, appends the '.medusa' extension, and drops a ransom note named '!!!READ_ME_MEDUSA!!!.txt'. It is used in a double-extortion scheme.

tools.name: AnyDesk
tools.description: A legitimate remote management tool abused by Medusa actors for lateral movement and persistence.

tools.name: ConnectWise
tools.description: A legitimate remote management tool abused by Medusa actors for lateral movement and persistence.

tools.name: Splashtop
tools.description: A legitimate remote monitoring and management (RMM) software abused by Medusa actors for persistence and lateral movement.

tools.name: Atera
tools.description: A legitimate remote monitoring and management (RMM) software abused by Medusa actors for persistence and lateral movement.

tools.name: vssadmin
tools.description: The legitimate Windows utility vssadmin.exe was used by attackers to delete volume shadow copies to inhibit system recovery.

vulnerabilities.name: CVE-2026-1731
vulnerabilities.description: An unpatched vulnerability exploited by Medusa affiliates for initial access, sometimes within 24 hours of public disclosure.

identities.name: Healthcare Sector Organizations
identities.description: A primary target sector for the Medusa ransomware group.

identities.name: Defense Sector Organizations
identities.description: A critical infrastructure sector targeted by the Medusa ransomware group.

identities.name: Manufacturing Sector Organizations
identities.description: A critical infrastructure sector targeted by the Medusa ransomware group.

identities.name: Government Sector Organizations
identities.description: A critical infrastructure sector targeted by the Medusa ransomware group.

infrastructure.name: Medusa Dark Web Leak Site
infrastructure.description: A dark web site used by the Medusa group to publish stolen data from victims who do not pay the ransom. It features a public countdown timer for each victim.

infrastructure.name: Medusa Exfiltration Storage
infrastructure.description: Attacker-controlled storage infrastructure used to house sensitive data exfiltrated from victim networks prior to encryption.

indicators.name: VSSAdmin Shadow Copy Deletion
indicators.pattern:
title: VSSAdmin Shadow Copy Deletion
id: 5e9b8f7a-1c3d-4b8e-9f6a-2d1c0b9e8f7a
status: experimental
description: Detects the use of vssadmin.exe to delete volume shadow copies, a common technique used by ransomware to inhibit system recovery.
references:
  - https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/cisa-medusa-ransomware-hit-over-500-critical-infrastructure-orgs/amp/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-08-20
tags:
  - attack.t1490
  - attack.impact
level: high
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '\vssadmin.exe'
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - 'delete'
      - 'shadows'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects attempts to delete volume shadow copies using vssadmin.exe, a behavior associated with Medusa ransomware to prevent recovery.

indicators.name: Medusa Ransomware File Artifacts
indicators.x_netsecio_sigma_rule:
title: Medusa Ransomware File Artifacts Creation
id: 8c4d5e6f-7b8a-4d9c-8a1b-2c3d4e5f6a7b
status: experimental
description: Detects the creation of Medusa ransom notes or files with the .medusa extension.
references:
  - https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/cisa-medusa-ransomware-hit-over-500-critical-infrastructure-orgs/amp/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-08-20
tags:
  - attack.t1486
  - attack.impact
level: critical
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_note:
    TargetFilename|endswith: '\\!!!READ_ME_MEDUSA!!!.txt'
  selection_ext:
    TargetFilename|endswith: '.medusa'
  condition: 1 of selection_*
indicators.description: Detects the creation of Medusa ransomware artifacts, such as the ransom note '!!!READ_ME_MEDUSA!!!.txt' or files encrypted with the '.medusa' extension.

indicators.name: Medusa RMM Tool Execution
indicators.x_netsecio_sigma_rule:
title: Medusa RMM Tool Execution
id: 9a8b7c6d-5e4f-4a3b-b2c1-d0e9f8a7b6c5
status: experimental
description: Detects the execution of legitimate RMM tools known to be abused by Medusa ransomware actors.
references:
  - https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/cisa-medusa-ransomware-hit-over-500-critical-infrastructure-orgs/amp/
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-08-20
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate administrative use of these RMM tools.
level: medium
tags:
  - attack.t1219
  - attack.command_and_control
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\\AnyDesk.exe'
      - '\\Splashtop.exe'
      - '\\AteraAgent.exe'
      - '\\ConnectWiseControl.Client.exe'
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Detects the execution of legitimate remote management tools like AnyDesk, Splashtop, Atera, and ConnectWise, which are abused by Medusa actors for persistence and lateral movement.
